components.css: :host{--ground:#ffffff;--ink:#1d1a26;--ink-2:#4b465a;--rule:#ddd6ea;--course:#6a2db0;--course-deep:#4f1f87;--course-tint:#efe6fa;--contour:#a8865a;--display:"Barlow Condensed","Barlow",sans-serif;--text:"Barlow",sans-serif;--ease:cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1);} .ds-dates{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;font:400 0.95rem/1.45 var(--text);color:var(--ink);font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;} .ds-dates li{display:grid;grid-template-columns:22px 104px 1fr;gap:10px;padding:0 0 14px;position:relative;} .ds-dates li::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:10px;top:14px;bottom:0;border-left:3px solid var(--course);} .ds-dates li.ds-ny::before{border-left-style:dashed;border-left-width:2px;} .ds-dates li:last-child::before{display:none;} .ds-dot{width:22px;height:22px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--course);margin-top:2px;box-sizing:border-box;} .ds-ny .ds-dot{background:#fff;border:2px dashed var(--course);} .ds-when{font:600 1.05rem/1.25 var(--display);} .ds-state{display:block;font:500 0.8rem/1.3 var(--display);letter-spacing:0.05em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-2);}

components.name: Process Map Course
components.description: Terrain bands with dashed contours; the reader's course from start triangle through numbered controls to the finish flag.

narrative.overview:
The law is drawn as orienteering terrain: the same flat, slanted bands of tint for every reader, one band per stage of the act, separated by dashed contour lines. Over it runs one purple course, the reader's route for their role, from a start triangle through numbered controls (each an article with its citation) to a finish flag. Everything that belongs to the reader wears the purple; everything that belongs to the law is ink on white or a flat terrain tint.

The page is a white, dense, calm reading surface. A condensed sans carries display text and labels with an engineered, map-legend voice; a quiet humanist sans carries the reading text with tabular figures so dates and identifiers line up. Depth is almost absent: hairline rules divide regions, one floating box sits over the map, and state is shown by the form of a line (solid or dashed) with a word beside it. Nothing is decorated for its own sake; the citation line under each fact is part of the design, not a footnote to it.

It rejects the legal database's sidebar tree over a wall of text, and the look of an institutional EU portal.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, ink text, hairline violet-grey rules.
Six flat stage tints in slanted bands with dashed contour boundaries: the terrain.
One purple, the course: route, controls, active role, links, primary action, wordmark.
Barlow Condensed for display and labels, Barlow for reading, tabular figures throughout.
State by line form plus a label: solid means applies or in force, dashed means not yet.
A citation under every fact; unchecked content visibly labelled; the two notices in every footer.

rules.name: The Reader's Purple Rule
rules.body: Purple belongs to the reader: the course, its controls, the active role, links, the primary action, focus and selection, and the wordmark. Headings, labels, table headers and the law's own content are ink. Before painting anything purple, ask whose it is; if it is the law's, it is ink or a terrain tint.

rules.name: The Flat Terrain Rule
rules.body: Stage tints are flat fills with dashed contour boundaries. No gradients, no shadows, no text colour drawn from a tint.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is set on the body; dates, article numbers and CELEX identifiers align in every table and timeline.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Condensed for what you scan (titles, headings, labels, numbers on the map), regular Barlow for what you read. Never set a paragraph in the condensed face.

rules.name: The Only Float Rule
rules.body: Shadow means "this sits on top of the map". A card on the white page gets a hairline border, never a shadow.

rules.name: The Line Form Rule
rules.body: State is carried by the form of a line plus a word, never by colour alone. Solid is applies or in force; dashed is not yet. Every dashed state mark sits next to its label ("not yet", "Not yet:", "not yet reviewed").

dos: Do keep purple for the reader: course, controls, active role, links, primary action, focus, selection, wordmark. Headings, labels and table heads are ink.
Do show state with line form plus a word: solid for applies or in force, dashed for not yet.
Do put a cite line under every fact, and label unchecked content with the dashed state tag or a plain "not yet" line.
Do end every page with both notices: information, not legal advice; independent, not affiliated with the European Union.
Do draw the law's stages as flat terrain tints with dashed contour boundaries, and the role as a purple course of start triangle, numbered controls and finish flag.
Do set dates and identifiers in tabular figures, and display text and labels in Barlow Condensed.
Do divide regions with 1px hairlines; reserve shadow for something floating over the map.
donts: Don't colour headings, section labels or the law's content purple.
Don't signal state by colour alone; a dashed line without its word is not enough.
Don't show a fact without its citation, or show unchecked content without its label.
Don't shade, gradient or texture the terrain tints, or use them as text colours.
Don't set paragraphs in the condensed face.
Don't fall back to a sidebar tree over a wall of legal text.
